chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn Al-Lu'lu'i, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Mu'az Al-Jawhari, from Amr ibn Jamee'a, who linked it up through his chain to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).

He said: Using the miswak (tooth-stick) contains ten characteristics: It purifies the mouth, it pleases the Lord, it multiplies good deeds seventy times over, and it is from the Sunnah. It removes cavities and whitens the teeth, strengthens the gums, cuts the phlegm, removes the haze of vision, and stimulates the appetite.

key_terms.السِّوَاكُ: The act of using a tooth-stick for oral hygiene

ai.seo_question: What are the ten benefits of using the miswak according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* underscores the dual nature of the miswak as both a physical purifier and a means of spiritual elevation, reflecting the Shia emphasis on integrating bodily hygiene with worship. It highlights the prophetic tradition's view that mundane acts, when performed with intention, yield multiplied rewards, specifically noting the seventy-fold increase in good deeds alongside tangible health benefits like strengthened gums and improved vision.
